propositions: Gerrit CI applies the workflow definition from the target branch but checks out the change's tree, causing newly-added gate steps to fail when the referenced script does not exist in older changes.
Gate steps invoking scripts unconditionally hard-fail with 'No such file or directory' for changes landing before the script was introduced.
Both new gate steps (raw-git-write and wall-clock-assert) must guard script invocation with an existence check and skip with a logged message when the script is absent from the checked-out tree.
The workflow must include inline documentation of the guard idiom and the definition-from-target-branch vs. change-tree skew rationale so future gate authors adopt the same pattern.
Guard implementation must propagate exit codes when script is present and return exit 0 when skipping due to script absence.
